title: MBBSDASM — segmented NE disassembler

title: RUST/SJ — RT-11-compatible PDP-11 OS sources

reason: Native 6809 recreation of the 1971 discrete-logic arcade game. reason: Button-driven native C reimplementation of Zork I with verb/noun selection and scrolling text. engine.c directly implements room/object accessibility, light sources, inventory, puzzles, score, troll/thief interactions and victory state; this is not a Z-machine CPU-wrapper port.

title: B Compiler Collection — x86-64 and BESM-6 language tools

title: DosGameMenu

title: Sam Nasty — STOS game and level editor

title: ADiffView — native Amiga text comparison viewer
reason: A native C++ side-by-side text-file difference viewer with an Amiga GUI, Myers-derived diff engine, selection/search/navigation and background worker code.

title: Conway Squasher — historical coroutine assembly ports
reason: Reimplements the asterisk-squasher coroutine example from Melvin Conway’s 1963 compiler paper in modern x86/x86-64 assembly, with Linux, macOS and Windows versions, both subroutine and coroutine styles and smoke-test fixtures. title: DiskMaster2 — Amiga file manager source archive

title: NiKom — Amiga KOM-style BBS
reason: Niklas Lindholm’s Swedish KOM-model Amiga BBS, originally developed 1990–1996, later maintained by Tomas Kärki, and revived from NiKom 1.60 sources in 2015. Contains node/server code, conferences, file areas, Fido support and utility libraries.

title: Crawlers

title: Wolves
